sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Airport Bonded In-Flight Meal Production and Direct Ramp Delivery

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (EU-harmonised commercial and company law; written legal code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (1992), applicable if any ultimate beneficial owner is China-resident
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Convention on Income and Capital (1994), as amended, subject to limitation-of-benefits and principal-purpose test
European Union internal market and capital-movement freedoms for EU/EEA-resident ultimate owners
Full BIT/DTA/FTAA schedule to be locked after UBO residence is identified during the piercing stage

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on RBE filing and access; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on professional AML/CFT obligations; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies for SARL formation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of legal existence of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the source state is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the ultimate corporate shareholder authorising incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL and appointment of local representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / corporate secretary of the ultimate parent or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in the country of origin, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague source states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg notary and incorporation agent for RCS, RBE, and municipal licence filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chairman, managing director, or duly authorised corporate officer of the incorporating shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification declaration and beneficial ownership statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner as a natural person, with attestation by the AML/KYC officer of the incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or certified true copy; apostille/consular legalization required if the declaration is executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC identity package (certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each director, statutory manager, and UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant or notary in the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-EU documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all directors, statutory managers, shareholders, UBOs, and material aviation/catering counterparties against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, US OFAC SDN list, and domestic Luxembourg sanctions lists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence under FATF Recommendation 12 and Article 3 of the amended 12 November 2004 AML/CFT Law. Negative news and high-risk jurisdiction checks are mandatory before incorporation; records must be preserved for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online portal lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin script and may be in Luxembourgish, French, German, or English. Foreign-script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The SARL legal-form suffix must be included or clearly stated. RCS will refuse names that are confusingly similar, misleading, or incompatible with public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: a name-reservation request may be renewed before its 30-day expiry by submitting a new reservation request through LBR and paying the corresponding fee. Rejection: the RCS refusal notice will state the legal grounds; the applicant may file a reasoned administrative reconsideration with RCS within 15 days of refusal. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may appeal to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in commercial matters within one month of notification. For sensitive tokens, the applicant must first obtain the relevant sectoral ministerial approval or regulator waiver and then re-file the name application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual registered office is not acceptable for the SARL. Luxembourg law requires a fixed and identifiable physical address in Luxembourg. A licensed domiciliation provider may be used for administrative purposes, but the inflight-catering business requires a physical, leasehold kitchen and airport ramp-access location before the operating licence can be issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Once the catering licence application is filed, there is an approximately 85% probability of an unannounced food-safety and hygiene inspection within the first 12 months of operation, and a 90-95% probability of airport airside security vetting/inspection before ramp delivery authorisation is granted.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS preliminary name search, clearance, and reservation filing
Notarial deed for the SARL articles of association and share capital subscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Ministry of Justice notarial tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee, inclusive of deed drafting and signature formalities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and publication of the incorporation deed in the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration and publication fee under Luxembourg commercial registry rules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) filing and beneficial ownership disclosure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Luxembourg sanctions screening and due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Incorporation agent / licensed Luxembourg law firm AML compliance desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Stage 1 jurisdiction-hub due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalisation of corporate documents (estimated 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities and Luxembourg consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fees plus courier costs; average of USD 260 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation arrangement for the pre-licence and incorporation phase
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Six-month domiciliation market tariff; mandatory physical address for SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary commercial, food-safety, and airport catering licence application scheduling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent municipality / Luxembourg airport authority and health inspection body
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative licence application fee and sanitary inspection scheduling benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) regime under Articles 710-1 et seq. (Title V), together with relevant Luxembourg Business Registers regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif / Statuts de société) registered with the RCS through the LBR e-Desk platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum paid-up share capital, fully subscribed and paid-up in cash or in kind before RCS registration; cash capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution and released only after registration and board approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation resolutions and the draft articles of association of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée be and are hereby approved for filing; THAT the registered office of the company be established at [registered office address in Luxembourg]; THAT the paid-up share capital be accepted and the managers be authorized to release it from the blocked escrow account upon RCS registration; THAT [Name] be and is hereby appointed Manager with full day-to-day management authority; THAT the Manager be authorized to complete all regulatory filings, appoint the statutory auditor where required, and apply for all food-safety, environmental, civil-defense, and occupational licences necessary for the airline inflight catering kitchen; THAT the Manager may act singly for all banking and administrative purposes; THESE resolutions shall take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and legal due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search for the proposed corporate name on the LBR name index; reserve the name if such service is available; verify that the intended inflight catering activity is lawful and not prohibited; collect constitutional documents and confirm applicant identity details.
required_dossiers: Proposed articles of association (draft)
Identity documents of all subscribers and proposed managers
Proof of lawful business purpose (ISIC 5621 airline inflight catering)
Power of attorney if a representative acts for any subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, submit a new name application to LBR within the prescribed response window or appeal through the RCS registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocked capital escrow account and depositing minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorized to accept corporate formation escrow accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the company in formation at a bank licensed in Luxembourg; deposit the fully subscribed EUR 12,000 minimum share capital; obtain a blocked-funds certificate from the bank confirming that the funds are held solely for the company pending RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Subscriber identity and passport copies
AML/KYC forms and source of funds declaration
Bank account opening application
Beneficial ownership confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or AML queries, provide supplementary due diligence documentation and resubmit the file; if the bank refuses the account, select another licensed Luxembourg credit institution and repeat the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to review and finalize the articles of association; the notary verifies legal capacity, share subscription, minimum capital deposit, and validity of the business purpose; the deed is executed in notarial form and certified copies are issued for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final draft articles of association
Bank blocked-funds certificate for share capital
Name reservation confirmation or acceptance letter
Identity documents and residence proofs of all shareholders
Consent and confirmation of proposed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, obtain a supplementary shareholder resolution or amend the draft deed and re-execute the notarial instrument before submission to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via LBR e-Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, the LBR-2 registration form, proof of registered office, and manager information to the RCS through the LBR e-Desk; pay the applicable filing fee; upon approval, the RCS assigns the company registration number and the incorporation is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (certified copy)
LBR-2 registration form
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital deposit
Identity documents of managers
Registered office address proof or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rejection, respond with corrected documentation within the stated deadline, usually 15 days; if the rejection is confirmed, appeal to the competent administrative court or re-file after curing the formal defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security, and beneficial ownership registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des enregistrements, des douanes et des domaines (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, obtain the Luxembourg business tax and VAT numbers from the AED, register as an employer with the CCSS for payroll and social security obligations, and file beneficial ownership details with the LBR-managed register of beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Certified copy of the deed of incorporation
List of appointed managers and their ID documents
Bank account details of the formed company
Beneficial ownership information and supporting ownership chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED or CCSS requests clarifications, provide the requested corporate records and register the missing fields within the prescribed deadline; appeal or amend through the respective administrative portal if the refusal is maintained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), Direction générale de l'industrie et des services, in coordination with the relevant municipal authority for building and operating permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and food establishment approval / agrément sanitaire for the airline inflight catering kitchen

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 3 – environmental declaration (déclaration) under the amended environmental law and relevant Grand-Ducal regulations; full EIA report is not required for a standard airline inflight catering kitchen below large food-processing capacity thresholds, but a registration/declaration obligation applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must meet municipal sewer discharge limits and Directive 91/271/EEC requirements; grease traps and fat/oil separation are mandatory before discharge; kitchen exhaust and combustion emissions must comply with VOC limits (typically 50 mg C/Nm³ for regulated air streams) and with applicable EU best available techniques where the facility falls under industrial-emissions thresholds; food waste, used cooking oil, and animal by-products must be managed under EU Regulation No 1069/2009 and national waste handling rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the kitchen and production area; structural load inspection and building occupancy approval from the municipal authority; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering ventilation, electrical safety, hot-work risks, refrigeration safety, and workplace welfare facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Primary e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) with ACOSET business registration and VAT registration modules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first file the incorporation deed and obtain a legal entity identifier from the Luxembourg Business Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS). Through the MyGuichet portal, the SARL applies for a national company tax number (numéro d'identification, NIF) and, if engaged in taxable activities, for a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA, format LU + 8 digits). The application requires proof of RCS registration, articles of association, identification of directors and shareholders, description of intended activities, and the appointment of a local tax representative if applicable. VAT registration is typically completed online via MyGuichet and must be initiated before or simultaneously with the first taxable supply in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Luxembourg SARL is by default a resident corporate entity fully taxable in Luxembourg on its worldwide income. It is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IRC), the municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC), and the net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, IF). Territorial scope applies to non-resident companies, but a resident SARL may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains. No pass-through taxation is available to an SARL under domestic law; the entity is a separate taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide an elective check-the-box classification regime. Available statutory elections include: (i) the option for joint and several VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 59 of the VAT law, allowing related persons to be treated as one taxable person; (ii) the election for VAT on real estate leasing or other occasional transactions; (iii) the election for horizontal and vertical fiscal consolidation under Article 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (intégration fiscale), enabling resident group members and qualifying 75%-owned Luxembourg subsidiaries to consolidate taxable results; and (iv) certain ATAD-compliant hybrid mismatch declarations for cross-border arrangements. These elections require formal submission to the AEDT or ACD and must be documented in advance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover in Luxembourg for supplies of goods and services (small business exemption threshold). Cross-border supplies may trigger registration at lower limits, including the EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance sales threshold; inbound intra-EU acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000 per year require Luxembourg VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing clearance regime is currently imposed by the AEDT for domestic B2B or B2C supplies. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies for Luxembourg public-sector procurement, requiring electronic invoices in PEPPOL format ('e-invoicing'). For commercial export and airline catering transactions, electronic invoices are acceptable if they comply with EU Directive 2022/55 and Luxembourg VAT invoicing rules; digital stamps and government fiscal XML clearance are not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg SARL performing airline inflight catering may zero-rate supplies of goods (food, beverages, and ancillary provisions) loaded onboard aircraft operating on international routes, thereby qualifying as supplies for the fuelling and provisioning of aircraft operated by airlines where the aircraft is engaged in international transport or the goods are removed from the EU. This exemption/zero-rating is grounded in Article 148(a) of the EU VAT Directive and Article 36 of the Luxembourg VAT law, subject to direct evidence that the goods are transported outside the EU by the aircraft before consumption. Supplies to airlines for strictly intra-EU or domestic flights remain subject to standard or applicable domestic VAT rates. The supplier must retain proof of the aircraft origin, departure point, route, and the actual loading of the catering goods; simple domestic delivery without physical export does not qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation) or transit/exiting summary declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill/Air Coupon confirming the goods were loaded on the identified aircraft
Inward Remittance Certificate or documentary evidence of payment in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and unitary export contract with the airline
Proof of aircraft departure from EU territory and international flight routing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively audit export zero-rating claims and recharacterize invalid claims as taxable domestic supplies, clawing back the unpaid VAT for up to 5 years (extended to 10 years in the event of fraud or intentionally concealed transactions). A fraudulent export VAT claim attracts statutory late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, administrative penalties of up to 100% of the evaded VAT, and additional fines. In serious cases, criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) and the Criminal Code may lead to imprisonment and further judicial fines. The VAT authorities also apply a generalized anti-avoidance stance requiring robust evidential files; where documentation is incomplete, the reversal of zero-rating may be combined with joint and several liability for holders of the goods and any transport participants.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); principal macroprudential and eurosystem authority; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) regulates bank conduct, AML/CTF, and payment and settlement systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member. Under TFEU Articles 63-66 capital and payments are fully free. There is no exchange-control regime, no central bank approval for inbound investment, and no restriction on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted from an FX perspective. Only tax withholding aspects remain relevant, chiefly the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when the 10% participation threshold is met) and ordinary corporate income tax (combined rate approximately 24.94%).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion into EUR, and no statutory repatriation period. Exporters may freely hold foreign currency bank accounts abroad or in Luxembourg. ECB balance-of-payments reporting and Intrastat statistical declarations apply for the purpose of EU-wide economic statistics, but these are informational and do not constrain currency conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for offshore non-EEA digital EMI; Medium for EEA-authorized EMI using passporting into Luxembourg under the Luxembourg law of 1 November 2009 on payment services as amended. An EMI can collect client funds and execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers, but it cannot issue formal letters of credit, act as a settlement bank for aviation ramp deliveries, or provide treasury credit lines. For capital escrow and operational accounts of an airline inflight catering SARL, a licensed Luxembourg deposit-taking bank is mandatory to preserve UCP600 LC capability and to maintain a clean correspondent banking profile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CSSF-aligned remote onboarding is permissible in Luxembourg through ETSI-compliant video identification and qualified electronic signature, and is generally accepted by domestic banks for EEA-based directors. However, for non-EEA ultimate beneficial owners, shareholders resident in FATF high-risk jurisdictions, or any PEP status, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one physical meeting with directors or UBOs at the bank's Luxembourg office or its embassy-notarised representative. The capital escrow account activation may additionally trigger a telephone or video compliance interview before the first inward wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner chain showing non-EEA tax residence or pass-through ownership in a high-risk or grey-listed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised Luxembourg corporate excerpt (extrait du registre de commerce), a certified register of shareholders, an attestation from a Luxembourg accredited accountant or legal counsel identifying the UBO, a signed group structure diagram showing full ownership chain, articles of association, audited financial statements of the direct shareholder, a bank reference from the shareholder's home bank, and a written business plan explaining the catering concession and expected inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flags on aviation industry counterparties, including cash-intensive ramp fees, sanctions-restricted airlines, or a lack of verifiable airport landing slot contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit copies of the airline catering service agreement and airport concession, valid Ministry of Health food hygiene licence, ISIC 5621 operating permit, complete counterparty list with LEI numbers, evidence of bond/security deposits, full invoicing and payment schedules, and an independent compliance opinion confirming no goods or services originate from sanctioned destinations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a parent company with unclear source of funds or mismatched purpose codes, especially intra-group loans without transfer pricing documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase, a signed loan agreement (if applicable), group transfer pricing documentation (for loans) or a sworn statement confirming no repayment obligation (for equity), bank statements from the remitter showing the origin of funds, tax residence certificates of the parent and subsidiary, and a detailed fund-flow narrative explaining the economic purpose of the injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) for EEA remitters or SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA remitters. The payment purpose must state 'CAPITAL INCREASE' or 'EQUITY INJECTION', and the beneficiary must use the SARL's Luxembourg IBAN. Banks will require a shareholder resolution and updated RCS excerpt before accepting the credit. For non-EEA funds, the remitter should route via a reputable global correspondent bank to prevent sanctions screening delays. The bank will apply CSSF AML checks and ECB balance-of-payments coding to the transaction. Inbound wire verification is completed by matching the amount, IBAN, payment reference, and supporting corporate documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA suppliers, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant where immediate EUR liquidity is available. For non-EEA suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking and prior FX conversion. For larger or structured aviation supply contracts, use a commercial letter of credit (UCP600), including a confirming Luxembourg bank if the issuing bank is of lower credit quality. The documentary set for LC payments should include a commercial invoice, airway bill or ramp delivery note, packing list, bonded kitchen inventory certificate, and any required inspection certificate. For recurring monthly airline catering invoices under EUR 1 million, wire-based open account settlement is acceptable; for high-value initial setup or infrastructure purchases, a standby LC is preferred.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or restricted currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels): balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, annex, and management report (if applicable) with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date: shareholders' meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of the financial year-end; filing must occur within 1 month of approval (e.g., for a 31-Dec FYE: approve by 30-Jun, file by 31-Jul).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS formal notice followed by court application; court-ordered injunction with penalty payments; persistent non-filing can trigger judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS; managing directors risk personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual direct-tax return (form 700) covering Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IF), with supporting annual accounts schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard calendar-year deadline: 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 Dec 2025); professional e-filers receive published extension dates; documentation and transfer-pricing file must be retained with the return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory tax assessment (taxation d'office), late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for accounting or return irregularities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE) declaration: annual accuracy confirmation and re-filing within 1 month of any transfer or change in the shareholding or beneficial-ownership chain of the SARL.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) - Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed calendar year-end: initial filing within 1 month of incorporation; updates within 1 month (30 days) after any relevant change; annual accuracy reminder cycle applied by the RBE portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 500-1,250 per violation for the entity and its managers; legal prohibition on profit distributions until the RBE file is accurate and up to date; court orders may compel filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (re viseur d'entreprises agree) where a Luxembourg SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4m, net turnover above EUR 8.8m, and average 50 employees. Audit is also required for public-interest entities, regulated financial or licensed businesses, and group subsidiaries subject to consolidated-audit or lender covenants. An ISIC 5621 in-flight catering SARL below these thresholds files abbreviated unaudited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts (as amended, implementing Directive 2013/34/EU), using the Plan comptable normalise. EU-adopted IFRS is available for consolidated group reporting; individual statutory accounts remain under Luxembourg GAAP for a non-listed SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg operates a continuous-accuracy UBO regime rather than a calendar-year re-registration. A SARL must file the initial RBE declaration within 1 month of incorporation and must re-file within 1 month of any share transfer or change in the direct or indirect ownership chain, even where the same natural person remains the ultimate beneficial owner. The RBE sends periodic accuracy reminders; the SARL must confirm or correct the data upon each reminder, and profit distributions are legally prohibited until the RBE file is current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associes) - compulsory SARL register held at the Luxembourg registered office; records all share transfers.
Register of Directors/Managers (gerants) - list of managers, powers, and signatures kept at the registered office and mirrored at the RCS.
Minute Book - formal minutes of shareholders' general meetings and management decisions, kept at the registered office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 - 4,400 per annum (approx. EUR 1,500-4,000) for a standard SARL registered-office and corporate-secretarial package in Luxembourg, including filing support, statutory register upkeep, and a resident agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - 16,500 (approx. EUR 5,000-15,000) when a statutory audit is triggered by size thresholds, group or parent requirements, or airport catering license conditions; nil for a qualifying micro or small company filing abbreviated unaudited accounts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (up to 12% for certain assets), and special incentives for small and medium enterprises

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or eTVA portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 months after the end of the fiscal year (extensions possible upon request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions if applicable
Only expenses directly related to Luxembourg-source income are deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief or unilateral credit for foreign taxes paid
Ensure correct allocation of income and expenses under Luxembourg GAAP

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; late payment interest of 0.5% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties for gross negligence or fraud

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for ≥12 months; treaty rates may apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, submit Form 1000 (or specific withholding tax relief form) to the Luxembourg tax administration, attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's jurisdiction, and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. Approval must be obtained before payment to apply reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory; 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if qualifying). Interest: 25% statutory; 0% under EU directive (if qualifying). Treaty rates may further reduce these.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 450,000 for related party transactions (goods) and EUR 450,000 for services; Master File required if group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in certain activities (e.g., holding, financing, IP). For an inflight catering operation, substance is inherent through physical premises, staff, and operational activity. Must maintain adequate personnel, premises, and decision-making in Luxembourg to avoid shell company characterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to 100% of tax evaded; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000; imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment if involved in fraudulent acts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, or artificial arrangements to avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of tax benefits, recharacterization of transactions, penalties up to EUR 100,000; potential criminal charges for tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in sham arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures, inadequate customer due diligence, or suspicious transaction reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1 million for entities; imprisonment up to 5 years for responsible individuals
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal fines, disqualification, and imprisonment for willful AML breaches

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjustment, interest on underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant TP policies
